P1.evidence: Acknowledged the setter conversation and set expectations about repeating questions — 'I heard from Kim that you already had a very good conversation with him as well. Could be that I ask a few of the same questions' — which is a partial P1a; the notes themselves were never read back. Three-part frame, agreement taken ('Okay, gotcha'), open question run.

P2.evidence: Age, weight, height and body fat all captured; injuries asked directly and properly — 'any injuries besides that one that you've had that I need to know' — which surfaced the ankle and the wrist. Training and nutrition covered in real depth. Work only emerged late and incidentally, at 00:31:00, which matters because his work schedule turned out to be the main obstacle. The significant miss is P2c: the prospect volunteered 'my ketone levels were low. And my testosterone was also low' and the rep responded 'Can it maybe come from nutrition?' and moved on. No sleep or energy questions.

P3.evidence: Strong work. Pushed from 'six-pack' to a target body-fat number, ran the 1-10 physique scale, asked the bridge question — 'is there something deeper or a bigger reason' — and got the grandfather story, then dated it and drew out the role-model layer: 'When it comes to being that role model, I'm just curious, how does that sort of look like for you?' The reflection at 00:34:18 was clean. Weaker on driving through to legacy or identity; the rep accepted 'Yeah, I guess so' on the role-model point rather than pressing.

P4.evidence: Established the Built with Science programme, when he joined, and what he thinks is wrong with it. But the prospect blocked the root-cause line and the rep did not push through: asked why he is on this call after only a month, and got 'Because I'm in tune with the universe'. The gap was named only in technical terms — variation and form — never in terms of why he cannot get himself past 16%. The 'information isn't the problem' question was never asked, and it was the one this prospect most needed.

P5.evidence: Attempted and immediately defeated. 'how do you think that you would end up in like five to ten years from now' drew 'if I feel like I'm stuck in a rut I'm gonna figure out a new path... I will figure it out. I'm pretty smart.' The rep tried once more with 'It doesn't sound like you're the type to settle for less' and got 'Nope' — which is agreement, not consequence. No 'why not', no line in the sand. Against a competent self-directed prospect the phase produced nothing, and the price then had nothing to sit against.

P6.evidence: The 1-10 scale substituted for the commitment questions and returned 'I'm ready to get started. I'm just, like I said, I wouldn't be on a phone call. If I wasn't ready to get started.' The belief question was asked in a softened form ('would you agree with me that we're actually going to be able to get to that longevity aspect') and the all-in question was never asked. The prospect had already flagged the real constraint at 00:31:00 — weekend customers and 'if the money's calling me, I gotta go' — and the rep did not resolve it before pricing.

P11.evidence: No sale of the core programme, so most of P11 does not apply. Against the downsell that was agreed: payment was not collected, the prospect explicitly deferred to Monday, and the rep walked him through the Skool link and where to click but got no completion. The rep did push for immediate action twice after being told there was no time.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran correctly — 'let's say 6K just falls on your lap like this. Would you then actually be like, yes, let's just get this going?' → 'Well, yeah. I mean, if I had money like that, of course.' Permission was asked twice and eventually granted. But only two elements of the financial picture were taken — monthly capacity ('$75 and $100 a week... between $350 and $400 a month') and cash on hand ('No, no, not at this time. I'm taking care of other people'). No credit cards, no available credit, no investments, no credit score. The rep stopped and pivoted to the downsell rather than completing the play.

'Not the right time' was the substance of the objection — a three-month income gap while he studies for his aviation licence. No OD move was run at all. No 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no compounding-cost frame, no 'what if all you had to do was show up'. The rep accepted the timing constraint at face value and built the rest of the call around working within it.

The cheaper-alternative objection the playbook already documents as a script gap, in its purest form: 'I paid $200 for one year for Jeremy, you know, and it's through an app. It's AI-operated.' A functioning substitute at $200/year against a $6,000/6-month offer — a thirtyfold difference — raised by the prospect himself, and completely unaddressed. The rep's next move was to introduce a $200/month product without ever acknowledging that he had just been told $200 buys a year elsewhere.

notes: Phase 3 was the strong part — the grandfather story was properly earned. Two coachable failures. Phase 5 collapsed against a self-reliant prospect who genuinely will figure it out, and the rep had no second frame, so $6,000 landed with nothing behind it. And a $200/year competitor was named out loud and never answered, immediately before quoting $200/month — the price comparison the prospect is certain to make on Monday when he decides whether to sign up.
